height.note: Land and inland water: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (TanDEM-X 2011-2015, edited; 1 arc-second, about 30 m; EGM2008 heights like ETOPO), from the public AWS bucket. It replaced Terrarium (SRTM) after a comparison at the pad field (out/bake/earth/site-bake/glo30-vs-srtm-*.png): the SRTM surface carried a pebbly, blocky noise texture that does not follow the imagery (RMS finer than 30 m 0.23-0.28 m, median slope 2.2-2.7 deg on a flat gravel plain), GLO-30 is clean and shows the real channels (0.07-0.16 m, 0.5-1.2 deg). The source is finer than the parent level's vertices at levels 8-11 only (level 11 samples every 18 m), so sourceCoverage lists levels 8-11 and level 12 carries the level-11 procedural detail (ARCHITECTURE 10.2). despikeBelow also removes land vertices more than 30 m below the median of their 9 x 9 neighbourhood (the SRTM source had corrupt rows along 19.0 N). Sea floor of the ocean (WorldCover water connected to the open sea): within 1.5 km of the WorldCover coastline the deeper of a 1:50 ramp from that coast (a sand and gravel shore; held at its 30 m depth beyond 1.5 km) and ETOPO 2022 15 arc-second (seaFloorNearShore 'deeper', the lead's rule: ETOPO's coarse coast lies up to 1.3 km offshore of the real one along this coast and says -1 m there, so ETOPO counts only where it is itself sea deeper than the ramp), becoming ETOPO between 1.5 and 3 km. The 1:50 slope meets ETOPO's own offshore gradient without a sill (profiles 19.0-19.45 N in docs/handoff/site-bake.md); in the shallow bay south of the headland (ETOPO -10 m) the floor within 3 km of the shore is up to 20 m deeper than ETOPO.

watermask.note: Inland water (WorldCover water not connected to the open sea) is kept only where the land source is flat under it and it is a pond, not a speck: a component (20 m cells) whose height spread (5th to 95th percentile) exceeds 2.5 m, whose mean slope exceeds 5 deg, or whose area is under 2,000 m2 is land (dark rock on the headland's hills and dark specks beside roads that WorldCover reads as water).
